persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Joy, 63, the volunteer bookkeeper at Hope Scholars Fund, a small charity in Ohio that pays school fees for students in Kenya. The founder is worried a filing date like the IRS Form 990 will be missed, and today she asks you to put them all in one place.

challenge.intro: Now you are Joy at Hope Scholars Fund. The app is empty. Nobody will tell you which button to press — use what you learned. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Open Ahead of It · Nonprofit with the normal link (not the 🧪 test copy). If the welcome tour shows, tap 'skip the tour' → '✨ Start fresh with my own' → OK. If it does not show, scroll to the very bottom of the page and tap '🧹 Start fresh — erase this app’s data' → OK → OK. The page reloads. If a dark screen says 'Everyone has a list of things…', tap 'I'll explore on my own' at the bottom. You now see an empty list ('empty' at the top). If a small 'Got it ✓' box appears when you open a tab, just tap it.

tasks.text: Put the Form 990 on your list. Your charity's year ends in June, so this year it is due on 15 November 2026 — make that its date.
tasks.hint: It is in the Library under IRS. After adding it, open it on the Next page and change 'Next due', then Save.

tasks.text: Put the board meetings (with their written minutes) on your list. Kevin is the board secretary — make sure Kevin is told about it.

tasks.hint: Add it from the Library (Board). Open it and look for the box 'Who else needs to know'.

tasks.text: The money for Term 1 school fees must reach Kenya by 5 January 2027. It is not in the library. Add it yourself as 'School fees transfer'. If it is late, it costs real money.
tasks.check: (function(){try{var d=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('goodstanding_v1')||'null');if(!d||!d.items)return false;var f=function(s){return d.items.filter(function(i){return String(i.id).indexOf('djex')!==0&&String(i.n||'').toLowerCase().indexOf(s)>=0})[0]};var i=f('school fees');return !!i&&i.due==='2027-01-05'&&i.sev==='h';}catch(e){return false}})()
tasks.hint: Use the round orange ＋ button. Fill in the name and the date, and choose how bad it is to miss.

tasks.text: Today you finished this month's bank reconciliation (checking the bank statement against your records). Put it on your list and tell the app this month's job is done.

tasks.hint: Add it from the Library (Money habits), then find it on the Next page. Saving it is not enough — one of its buttons says the job is finished.

tasks.text: If you are away, someone else will use this list. Write on it that it belongs to Hope Scholars Fund.
tasks.hint: Look in the Hand-off tab, in the box 'Whose list is this?'. Tap outside the box after typing.

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: keeps a small charity's important filing dates in one place
reminds you before papers like the Form 990 are due, so the charity stays legal and tax free
another person can take over using the hand-off list

lines: This is Ahead of It, nonprofit edition. In the next few minutes you will see what it is for, who it is for, and how to use it.
Here is the everyday problem. A nonprofit stays tax-exempt only if certain papers go in on time, every year.
The big one is the IRS Form nine-ninety, the yearly report. Miss it three years in a row, and tax-exempt status is revoked automatically.
Then there is the state charitable registration, the annual report, board meetings with minutes, insurance renewals, and year-end letters to donors.
In a small nonprofit, two or three volunteers carry all of that, and nobody is in the office. So a date slips by quietly.
Ahead of It is for that small team: the founder, the treasurer, or the board secretary who ends up holding the calendar.
The big idea is simple. Every deadline lives on one calm page, and each one comes with its own reminder steps, starting thirty days before it is due.
At the bottom are four tabs: Next, Year, Library, and Hand-off. The round orange plus button adds something of your own.
Start with Library. It holds seventeen things small nonprofits actually face, grouped as IRS, State, Donors, Board, Insurance, Money habits, and Practical.
You will find Form nine-ninety, the state registration, donor letters, board minutes, and the monthly bank reconciliation. Tap one, and it goes on your list with a typical date.
Or tap the gold Quick setup button. It shows the whole library on one screen, with a tick box and a date beside each item.
Tick what is yours, fix any date you know, and tap Save my list. Two or three is a fine start.
Now the Next tab. This is your main page, sorted by what needs you first.
Overdue is at the top, then Do something now, then Next ninety days, then Later this year. When nothing is overdue, it simply says so.
Each item shows how many days until it is due, and the one step to take right now, like Gather what you need.
When you finish a step, tap step tick. When the whole filing is done, tap done tick, and the item moves to its next date by itself.
Something not in the library, like a grant report? Tap the round plus button.
Give it a name and a next due date, choose how often it repeats, and pick how bad a miss would be: No big deal, A hassle, or Costs real money.
You can also note what happens if you miss it, who else needs to know, and where the papers or login are kept. Then tap Save.
The Year tab shows the next twelve months on one page, colored by how costly each miss would be. Print it for the board, or add every date to your calendar.
The Hand-off tab is for when someone else steps in. It copies or prints one page: what is due, who to tell, and where things are.
It also has Save backup file, because everything lives on this one device. And here you write whose list this is.
Your first two minutes: open Quick setup, tick Form nine-ninety and your state registration, and put in your real dates.
Then glance at the Next tab once a week. If it says Nothing overdue, you are ahead of it.
Your list stays on this device. There is no account, no cloud, and nothing is sent to anyone.
Ahead of It, nonprofit edition costs twenty-nine dollars, once. No subscription.
And the round question mark button has the tour and help, any time. Profits help students in Kenya stay in school.
